packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, isolated image-only reader (Claude Code subagent)
text:
PACKET-10 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of
the text. One thing the images themselves show: a modern blue ink ownership
stamp "BIBL. UNIV. / GENT" on one end of strip A (image-004, image-005). That
is a holding-library stamp, not a text identification; I record it as visible
and infer nothing further from it. I opened only PROMPT.md and the twelve image
files of this packet (file names came from one directory listing of the packet
directories; packet.json was not opened).

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)

The packet holds TWO narrow horizontal parchment strips, each photographed on
both faces, each with one reduced overview and two overlapping native tiles:

  Strip A, face 1: image-001 (overview), image-002 (left tile), image-003
                   (right tile)
  Strip A, face 2: image-004 (overview), image-005 (left tile, with stamp),
                   image-006 (right tile)
  Strip B, face 1: image-007 (overview), image-008 (left tile), image-009
                   (right tile)
  Strip B, face 2: image-010 (overview), image-011 (left tile), image-012
                   (right tile)

Observations
- Both strips are c. 11 cm long and c. 2.5-3 cm high by the rulers, cut
  horizontally across a leaf, so each preserves only 5-6 consecutive lines in
  height but (potentially) a wide stretch horizontally. Each has vertical
  creases dividing it into panels (binding-guard folds). Strip A has a notched,
  pointed blank end (a tab).
- On each face only ONE end panel (about 2 cm wide) keeps crisp ink. The long
  central panel is heavily rubbed/glue-stained; ink survives there only as
  smears, a few letters and offsets.
- Script: an upright gothic bookhand of medium size on strip A (thick, dark
  grey-brown ink). Strip B has the same kind of hand in two sizes: a larger
  module ("cos ex..." on face 2) and lines of normal module; plus, on face 2,
  four very faint lines of a small cursive in pale ink between the larger
  lines (see below).
- Red: a short red horizontal stroke and a small red marginal mark in the
  centre panel of strip A face 2 (image-005, c. line 5); a faint red line in
  the centre of strip A face 1 (image-002/003); a red dot on strip B face 2
  (image-011). No legible rubric.
- Strip A face 1, line 4 opens with a paragraph-mark-like sign before
  "ſuſcepta". Strip B face 1 has a blank space of about two line-heights
  between its line 2 and the next full line, with a short word in smaller
  script indented at the right of that gap; the following line opens with a
  larger/taller initial letter (ſ or similar). Strip B face 2 line 1 is in a
  visibly larger module than the lines below.
- No running title is visible (top margins are not preserved). Whether the
  crisp end panels and the rubbed centre belong to one column or two cannot be
  seen: on strip A face 1 the text of the left panel runs straight on across
  the fold into the rubbed zone, so at least that much is one column.

Tentative interpretation (not observation)
- Strip B: the blank gap + indented small word + taller initial looks like a
  section break (end of one item, short heading/cue, new item). The larger
  line on face 2 could be a heading, an incipit line, or simply a different
  text grade (e.g. sung text vs. read text). Not decidable.
- The faint cursive on strip B face 2 looks like a later annotation in a
  different hand written in a blank area; tentative.
- A and B could come from the same leaf or book (similar hand and format) but
  nothing in the images proves it.

2. AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD
Selected: the crisp end panel of each of the four faces (all preserved lines);
the few legible words in the rubbed centre panels.
Unread: the centre panels of all four faces (roughly 5-6 cm each), where I see
line-traces but can only pick out isolated letters; the faint cursive lines on
strip B face 2 beyond a couple of letter-groups. Multispectral/UV images of
the centre panels would be the useful next step; an adjacent crop will not
help, the limit is abrasion.

3. TRANSCRIPTION
Line numbers count from the top of the named image. Top and bottom lines of
each strip are cut horizontally. "|" marks the vertical fold where crisp ink
gives way to the rubbed zone.

--- STRIP A, FACE 1 (image-002 = left tile; image-001 overview shows same) ---
image-002 L1: ...]n(?)[2-3 letters]p(?)[...            (only lower halves)
image-002 L2: ꝯ(?) ſextum(?) eci(?)[.] | [illegible]   (alt. "ſextimū";
              first sign is a small hooked mark at the left edge)
image-002 L3: [.]tulant(ur)(?) d(?)[.] | [illegible]   (first letter c or t:
              "culantur"/"tulantur"; a 2-shaped sign or "z" after "tula")
image-002 L4: ¶(?) ſuſcepta d(?)[.] | [illegible]      (alt. "ſuſceptaq(ue)")
image-002 L5: ꝑ(?) pľam(?) ac(?)[..] | [illegible]     (alt. "ꝑ piam ac";
              first sign a p with stroke at the cut edge)
image-002 L6: [.] pace(?) ſurſ(?)[.] | [illegible]     (lower parts cut;
              alt. "par ſurſ-")
Centre and right (image-002 right half, image-003): 6 line-traces continue
for c. 6 cm; isolated shapes only (minims, an "a", a possible "ꝑ"); a short
red horizontal line at about L5. [illegible]. The right-hand end panel of
image-003 is blank parchment (the tab), with blind impressed/offset marks at
the far right edge but no ink text.

--- STRIP A, FACE 2 (image-006 = right tile; image-005 = left tile) ---
Crisp end panel (image-006, right):
image-006 L1: ...][illegible] d(?)om(?)[...           (only lower halves)
image-006 L2: ...]ſ(?)ic(?)uto(?) ut gau(?)[...       (alt. "dicito ut gau-";
              the first word is rubbed, "-uo/-to ut" is clear, then g + 2-3
              minims)
image-006 L3: ...]uiget(?) in h̄(?) u(?). alli(?)[...  (an abbreviation stroke
              with a flourish stands over the h; alt. for the end: "all'a")
image-006 L4: ...][.]m(?) ples(?) ſurſu(?)[...        (alt. "... ꝑles ſurſu-")
image-006 L5: ...]ind(?)[.]u(?)roꝛiu(?)[...          (alt. "in decoꝛoꝛ(um)";
              the middle is rubbed, "-oꝛoꝛiu/-oꝛoꝛu" with two round-r forms is
              the clear part)
image-006 L6: ...][.]uiſicio(?)[...                    (upper halves only; alt.
              "-niſtcio-", "-mſicio-")
Rubbed centre (image-005 right half / image-006 left half; the two tiles
overlap here, the words below are the same ones seen in both):
image-005 L4 (approx.): ...]nus(?) · ex(?)[2-3 letters]n(?)[...
image-005 L5 (approx.): ...] · ſp̄(?)ctabil(?)[...] (alt. "ſpetiali-",
              "ſpectabili-"; uncertain), with a short red stroke beneath and a
              small red mark in the left margin of the panel
image-005 L6 (approx.): ...][illegible]lec(?) · [illegible]
image-006 L1 (centre, top edge): ...]as(?) dim(?)[...
Left end (image-005): blank tab with the modern stamp "BIBL. UNIV. / GENT".

--- STRIP B, FACE 1 (image-008 = left tile; image-009 = right tile) ---
image-008 L1: ...][tails of letters only, top line cut]
image-008 L2: [.]ibꝫ(?) diſſe(?)[..]ntal(?)[.] | [illegible]
              (first word ends in "-ib" + us/et-sign; second word begins
              "diff-/diſſ-", middle rubbed, a tall l or ſ before the fold)
image-008 L3: [blank at left]        tu(?)[2-3 letters]t(?) | [illegible]
              (a short word in smaller script, set in from the left by about
              2 cm, at the fold)
[blank space of about one further line height at left]
image-008 L4: ſ(?)[.]ioli(?) appellet(?)[..] ... | [rubbed] ...ꝛc(?)
              (opens with a taller letter with a long curved head-stroke;
              "appell-" is fairly clear; alt. first word "ſcioli", "ſtoli")
image-008 L5: [upper tips of letters only, bottom line cut]
Centre and right (image-008 right half, image-009): dark, stained; 4-5
line-traces, nothing legible. Right end panel (image-009): blank.

--- STRIP B, FACE 2 (image-012 = right tile; image-011 = left tile) ---
image-012 L1 (larger module): ...][.]it(?). cos(?) exim(?)ia(?)[...
              (letters "cos ex" + five or six minims + "a" are clear; the
              minim group may be -imia-, -inna-, -unna-; first letter of "cos"
              could be e: "eos")
image-012 L2-L5: four lines of very faint small cursive in pale ink,
              apparently a different (later?) hand:
              L2: ...]erat(?) [illegible] ... ea(?)[...
              L3: ...][illegible]lect(?)[...
              L4: ...][illegible]
              L5: ...][illegible] ... t(?)[illegible]
image-012 L6: ...]aut(?)a(?) [gap, rubbed] [.]ms(?) . mapꝛ(?). · [space] mt(?) . a(?)[...
              (alt. for the clear group: "ma ꝑꝛ.", "mapz."; these look like a
              run of short abbreviated items separated by points)
image-012 L7: ...]us(?) ſ(?)[...] [.]ſc(?)riptoli(?)[...   (upper halves only,
              bottom line cut; alt. "-ſ(er)uoli-")
Left tile (image-011): rubbed panel with 5-6 line-traces, a darker blot of
ink near the top right ("...us/...uſa(?)" beneath it), and one red dot at
about the 5th line; [illegible]. Far left: blank end.

4. LIMITATIONS
- Every line is a fragment: the readable end panels give c. 8-12 letters per
  line, and I cannot connect them across the rubbed centre.
- Top and bottom lines on every face are cut through horizontally.
- I cannot establish which face is recto/verso, nor the order of strips A and
  B, nor whether they join.
- Minim groups are ambiguous throughout; alternatives are listed rather than
  resolved. No word has been supplied from sense.
- This is an unverified image reading. I did nothing beyond the stated rules
  other than the directory listing noted above.
